block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Waterfront fit depends on whether the location premium creates real lifestyle or market value. For European buyers, compare the price premium, view durability, access, service charges, maintenance exposure, obstruction risk and future competing supply. Pay for the premium only when the benefit is clear enough to matter in actual use or at resale.

items.answer: Waterfront fit depends on whether the location premium creates real lifestyle or market value. For European buyers, confirm the floor, orientation and actual line of sight rather than assuming every unit in a waterfront or view-led project has the same outlook.
items.question: How should I assess whether waterfront property fits my needs?

items.answer: A view premium is justified only when the view is durable and valued by future buyers. Review adjacent plots, planned phases and infrastructure that could change an open view or the perceived waterfront position later.
items.question: How should I assess whether a view premium is justified?

items.answer: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. Review sunlight, privacy, noise, neighbouring buildings and the direction of important rooms instead of evaluating the plan in isolation.
items.question: What should I check in a floor plan?

items.answer: Unit size should be compared through usable space and layout efficiency, not area alone. Test whether the extra or reduced space changes household comfort, tenant appeal or resale demand enough to justify the price difference.
items.question: How should I compare unit sizes?

items.answer: Project location should be judged at street and access level, not only by district name. The project sits in a less convenient or less desirable part of an otherwise attractive area. Verify the exact location because two projects in the same area can offer very different day-to-day quality.
